messages:
Marta (support): customer says p99 spiked to ~600ms for /v1/generate since 08:58 UTC. They claim they pinned region=us-east-1 but traces show a hop into eu-west-1. customer request ids: r_01FJ9A, r_01FJ9B. Can SRE look?

Sam (SRE): copying in priya/alex. Do we have the request-level routing trace? ask customer for their x-trace header or curl they used.

Marta (support): they sent this curl and headers:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ak_live_..." \ 
  -H "x-redwood-region: us-east-1" \ 
  -H "x-request-id: r_01FJ9A" \ 
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```
They also pasted an excerpt from their trace-beacon showing a weird intermediate hop: trace: 01-abc-...

Priya (eng): I pulled the internal route decision using the request id. Found this in routing logs: 
```
route_decision_id=rd-8745 request_id=r_01FJ9A selected_region=eu-west-1 fallback_reason=capacity_shortage selected_model=model-ggml-eu variant=quantized added_latency_ms=380
```
This suggests an automated fallback to an EU variant despite the client header.

Alex (platform): hm — fallback policy should respect explicit x-redwood-region pin unless the pinned model is unavailable and the policy is set to "region-strict:false" for the customer org. Checking org config for acme-app.

RouteBot: org_config for org=acme-app: region_preference=us-east-1 region_strict=false fallback_regions=[eu-west-1,us-west-2] autoscale_status=at_capacity in us-east-1

Sam (SRE): that matches. Autoscaler reported GPU pool for the requested model at 100% at 08:56 UTC and an on-the-fly fallback was triggered. Unfortunately the route decision didn't annotate the response with a clear header to the client. We can repro locally with a short script (forcing pool saturation).

Priya (eng): repro steps I used:
1) spawn 8 concurrent long-context generations to saturate us-east-1 pool for model-ggml-us
2) send a follow-up request with x-redwood-region: us-east-1 and small payload
3) watch routing log show fallback to model-ggml-eu and added ~350-420ms RTT

Example script snippet:
```
# saturate pool
for i in $(seq 1 8); do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer ak_test" -d '{"prompt":"long loop"}' &
done
# then single request
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "x-redwood-region: us-east-1" -H "Authorization: Bearer ak_test" -d '{"prompt":"quick"}'
```

Sam (SRE): action items: 1) short-term: add explicit response header when fallback occurs (x-redwood-fallback: eu-west-1) so customers see it immediately. 2) medium: make region_strict default true for orgs that explicitly set region header. 3) notify customer and credit for the delta. I'll open an incident ticket.

Alex (platform): I created a config change PR to default region_strict=true when user supplies x-redwood-region header. Also adding a metric to track cross-region fallbacks per org.

Marta (support): told customer we've identified reason: autoscale fallback into eu-west-1 due to capacity. Asking if they'd prefer we block cross-region fallbacks entirely or increase reserved capacity for their org. Offering a 2-day credit for increased latency.

Priya (eng): also note: route decision needs to log the exact fallback model variant and provide the trace-id in system logs; I added that to the PR.

Sam (SRE): incident ticket INF-2026-324 created. Patch to add header + logging pushed to staging. Will run canary tonight at 02:00 UTC.

Marta (support): customer updated: wants region lock. I set org_config.region_strict=true for acme-app as a stop-gap. Monitoring for drops. :thumbsup:

Alex (platform): follow-up: plan to ship the header change and config default in the next deploy window. Also we should update docs to explain fallback behavior and the x-redwood-fallback header.

Marta (support): closing loop with customer in 30m and will paste final logs. Thanks team. :wave:
